stem: A status chart uses red and green circles to show pass and fail. Which test best checks whether the meaning survives without color?

options.rationale: Grayscale removes the color difference, so any status that becomes ambiguous was relying on color alone.

options.text: Check that the chart's labels have enough contrast against the background.
options.rationale: Label contrast affects readability but does not show whether the red and green circles still convey status without color.

options.text: Ask several colleagues if the two colors are visible.
options.rationale: Visibility says nothing about whether the status is still identifiable without color.

options.text: Run an HTML validator and confirm the chart markup is well formed.
options.rationale: Valid markup can still use color as the only way to convey meaning.

explanation: WCAG's use-of-color requirement says color must not be the only visual means of conveying information. Viewing the chart in grayscale is a quick check: if pass and fail become indistinguishable, add text, a pattern, or a shape. Contrast checks and markup validation do not test color dependence.

references.title: W3C WAI — Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.1: Use of Color

author: Oxypteros
